# Leverage ranking: functions and data by unique-body references

Generated by `tools/leverage_rank.py` with `docs/leverage.tsv` (one row per unit, sorted by score). `leverage_rank.py --check` regenerates both in memory and byte-compares them.

## Inputs
- `build/`: linker maps, ELFs and .o files of 218 binaries; 7428 objects (7355 placed, 73 unlinked).
- `.run/sig.<alias>.jsonl`: 362389 sig rows (h_exact per function instance).
- `.run/P37/census/struct_map.json` (`tools/type_census.py`): 14376 type entries, 13937 distinct names (same-named entries are one C name and merge).
- `.run/P37/census/sites.jsonl` (`tools/type_census.py --sites`, same run): 531366 site rows, 255394 typed by a struct_map type (`type`, or a C-form `ctype` naming one).
- The tool refuses to run when `git diff --quiet <census head> HEAD -- src include` fails (regenerate the census first); the head is not printed here, so a census regenerated at a new HEAD with unchanged src/include keeps `--check` green.

## Columns
- `key`: h_exact[:12] (func), `raw:<space>:<addr>` (func with no sig row), `<space>:<addr>` (data). `space`: vram base of the image holding the address (`abs` outside every image). `addr`: exemplar address. `named`: yes/partial/no. `refs`: unique-body references. `bodies`: distinct source bodies. `nins`: instructions of the body (sig funcs only). `addrs`: distinct instance addresses. `fan`: instances (func) or referencing binaries (data). `binaries`: referencing binaries. `own`: struct ownership credit. `owner`: the held type of largest reach. `rank43`: rank among the units 3.43 may name.

## Method
- Every relocation of every object (all sections) is attributed to a source body and a target unit, or to a named exclusion; unattributed must be 0. A text source body is the sig row containing the place (h_exact, offset), so a body linked into many binaries counts once; a data source is the nearest preceding data symbol of its output section.
- Units: `func` = one h_exact (every instance of one body); `func` `raw:<space>:<addr>` = a target with no sig row that starts an ELF FUNC or global symbol; `data` = (space, addr). Space: the binary's own image (its VRAM base), else main's, else resident's, else another image's slot base, else `abs`.
- References are deduplicated to unique-body keys (source body, offset, reloc type, target unit); HI16 halves are counted once through their LO16.
- Struct ownership: each typed site's body (tu, fn) maps to the h_exact it compiles into (non-header: the TU's alias and the function's address; a `src/shared/**` header: every include site in src with its active `SHARED_FN`, nested includes followed). reach(T) = distinct h_exact over all sites typed T. holders(T) = distinct data units named by a global/gaddr site typed T, plus T's `globals_at`/`globals_ptr`, resolved through the TU alias's symbols, then the space rule.

## Weights
`score = (refs + own) x (1 + log10(fan))`, printed with 3 decimals; ties by refs, kind, key.
- **refs**, 1 per unique-body reference: one occurrence of the name in the one-text-per-body source, so one rename rewrites exactly refs sites.
- **own** = sum over struct types T held by the unit of reach(T) / holders(T): a global is where a struct type gets its name, and every body using the type reads that name; the reach is split among the holders so each type is credited once.
- **fan factor** `1 + log10(fan)` (fan = instances for a function, referencing binaries for a datum): a name reaches every instance's symbol stack and Ghidra view for one decision but adds no source occurrence. Damped, not linear: `nins x reach` over-counted (docs/decision-log.md:1655-1667).

## Known limits
- Param-typed structs credit no unit: a type seen only through parameters and locals has reach but no holder.
- Slot-space conflation: overlays sharing a VRAM base share one space, so `data` and `raw:` units at the same slot address in different overlays pool into one unit.
- `abs` space: targets outside every image (main's bss past its last section, fixed addresses) form one space with no binary.
- `globals_at`/`globals_ptr` are capped at 20 names per type; the full holder set comes from the sites.
